title: Rambutan Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Rambutan Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Rambutan nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen and potassium in rambutan, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Rambutan nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your rambutan turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus, zinc and magnesium. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Potassium deficiency on a leaf, shown on another crop as a stand in for rambutan

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But zinc stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which rambutan nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a rambutan nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest rambutan nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in rambutan

No rambutan particular description was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs. The canopy turns light green, then the older leaves yellow evenly and drop, and the yellowing moves up. New flushes after harvest come out short with small leaves, so the tree has less leaf to carry the next crop. You see it most at this stage: after harvest, when the tree should flush, and in young trees.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in rambutan
Rambutan removes a lot of nitrogen with its fruit and the twigs cut at harvest. Trees fed only organic matter or nothing at all, sandy soils and heavy rain show it most.
How to tell it apart

Glyphosate sprayed under the canopy edge causes severe yellowing and drop of lower leaves, as the ICRAF tree database warns. Ask what was sprayed. To be sure, leaf test of the last fully mature leaflets on branch tips, taken before flowering. Queensland researchers suggest 2.0 to 2.5 percent nitrogen as the target range.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

For young trees in the third and fourth year, the DA Cagayan Valley guide gives 1 to 2 kg of complete fertilizer per tree with 300 grams of Muriate of potash. For bearing trees it gives 25 kg of organic fertilizer per tree after ring weeding, then 2 to 3 kg of Complete 14 14 14 or 16 20 0 one to two months later. The ICRAF tree database gives about 200 grams of nitrogen per tree for each year of age, up to 12 years, with half of the yearly amount right after harvest. Too much nitrogen can delay flowering and make fruit drop.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, feed the tree right after harvest to push a good flush, and return pruned twigs and leaves as mulch.
Potassium deficiency in rambutan

No rambutan particular description was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs. Edges and tips of older leaflets yellow, then dry brown, and the scorch moves inward. Fruit set is poorer and fruits stay small and less sweet. You see it most at this stage: fruit growth, when the crop pulls the most potash.
Why potassium deficiency happens in rambutan
Rambutan removes a lot of potassium with its fruit. Leached, sandy soils under heavy rain, and trees fed mostly nitrogen, show it most.
How to tell it apart

Rambutan is very sensitive to chloride. Queensland researchers link leaf edge burn and leaf drop mostly to too much chloride, for example from Muriate of potash. To be sure, leaf test of the last fully mature leaflets on branch tips before flowering, for both potassium and chloride. Queensland researchers suggest 0.7 to 0.9 percent potassium and chloride below 0.2 percent.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

The DA Cagayan Valley guide gives 300 grams of Muriate of potash with the complete fertilizer before flowering. A second potash dose in water during fruit growth for bigger, sweeter fruit. Because rambutan dislikes chloride, Queensland researchers advise Sulfate of potash or potassium nitrate instead. Switch to those where leaf edges burn. The ICRAF tree database gives about 130 grams of potash per tree for each year of age for fruiting trees, up to 12 years.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, split potash between before flowering and fruit growth, and choose a chloride free source on trees that show edge burn.
Phosphorus deficiency in rambutan

No rambutan particular description was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs. The tree grows slowly and stays stunted, and older leaves turn dull with a purple or bronze tint, mostly underneath. Flowering is weak. You see it most at this stage: young trees, and the weeks before flowering in bearing trees.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in rambutan

Very acid soils that hold phosphorus tightly, and soils low in organic matter. Rambutan needs less phosphorus than nitrogen and potash, but leaf surveys in Queensland still found some trees below the suggested range.
How to tell it apart

Drought, cold and root damage can also slow growth and tint leaves. Nitrogen deficiency gives pale yellow, not purple, old leaves. To be sure, leaf test of the last fully mature leaflets on branch tips before flowering. Queensland researchers suggest 0.2 to 0.3 percent phosphorus.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

The DA Cagayan Valley guide uses Complete 14 14 14 or 16 20 0 before flowering, which supply phosphorus. In a Thai trial, a leaf spray of monopotassium phosphate at 5 grams per liter, three times a week apart once the last flush matured, followed by a 7 13 34 foliar feed with zinc, gave the most flowering, about 10 days earlier than unsprayed trees. Follow the soil test and lime very acid soils.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, put phosphorus and compost in the planting hole and keep some in the yearly program.
Zinc deficiency in rambutan

No rambutan particular leaf description was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs. New leaflets are small and narrow, yellow between the veins, and crowd at the shoot tip. In a Thai trial, trees with more leaf zinc made more flower panicles per shoot. So a shortage shows up as weak flowering and fewer fruits. You see it most at this stage: the last flush before flowering, and flowering.
Why zinc deficiency happens in rambutan
Sandy or eroded soils, high pH or overlimed soils, and heavy phosphate fertilizer. Queensland leaf surveys found some orchards below the suggested zinc range.
How to tell it apart

Iron and manganese deficiency also yellow young leaves between the veins, but the leaves keep their size. Mites and thrips can stunt and curl new leaves. To be sure, leaf test of the last fully mature leaflets on branch tips before flowering. Queensland researchers suggest 30 to 35 ppm zinc.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

Spray zinc on the mature last flush before flowering. In the Thai trial, a 7 13 34 foliar fertilizer containing zinc, at 1.5 grams of product per liter and sprayed three times a week apart, gave the biggest panicles. Zinc sulfate also works. TNAU sprays for other fruit trees use 3 to 5 grams Zinc sulfate per liter. Follow the label.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester, Inc. (22 percent zinc), **Great Planters Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (21 percent zinc), **Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** by Petbowe Trading Corporation (33 percent zinc) and **YaraVita ZINTRAC 700** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (40 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, avoid very heavy phosphate and overliming, and check leaf zinc every few years.
Magnesium deficiency in rambutan

No rambutan particular description was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs. Older leaflets yellow between the veins while the veins stay dark green. In bad cases growth slows, new leaves are smaller and lower leaves drop. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees, often during and after fruit growth.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in rambutan
Acid, leached soils and heavy potash fertilizer, which competes with magnesium. Queensland leaf surveys found some orchards below the suggested magnesium range.
How to tell it apart

Potassium shortage or chloride burn scorches the leaf edges brown rather than yellowing between the veins. Nitrogen deficiency yellows the whole old leaf, veins included. To be sure, leaf test of the last fully mature leaflets on branch tips before flowering. Queensland researchers suggest 0.25 to 0.35 percent magnesium.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

The ICRAF tree database gives Dolomite at 0.4 kg per tree for each year of age, up to 10 years, applied in the slow growing months. Where the soil pH is already fine, use Magnesium sulfate or Kieserite, following the soil test.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use Dolomite when liming and keep potash and magnesium in balance.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any rambutan nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your rambutan needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Rambutan nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my rambutan leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: pale canopy, yellow older leaves that drop, and weak, short flushes after harvest. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in rambutan?
items.a: For young trees in the third and fourth year, the DA Cagayan Valley guide gives 1 to 2 kg of complete fertilizer per tree with 300 grams of Muriate of potash. For bearing trees it gives 25 kg of organic fertilizer per tree after ring weeding, then 2 to 3 kg of Complete 14 14 14 or 16 20 0 one to two months later.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in rambutan?
items.a: The DA Cagayan Valley guide gives 300 grams of Muriate of potash with the complete fertilizer before flowering. A second potash dose in water during fruit growth for bigger, sweeter fruit.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in rambutan?
items.a: The DA Cagayan Valley guide uses Complete 14 14 14 or 16 20 0 before flowering, which supply phosphorus. In a Thai trial, a leaf spray of monopotassium phosphate at 5 grams per liter, three times a week apart once the last flush matured, followed by a 7 13 34 foliar feed with zinc, gave the most flowering, about 10 days earlier than unsprayed trees.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my rambutan lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the rambutan nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
